articles.title: Milsinho anuncia lançamento de projeto novo da Toque Dez | G1
articles.standfirst: Banda foi uma das atrações a desfilar no Circuito Maneca Ferreira nesta quinta-feira (19), primeira noite da festa.
articles.summary: Banda foi uma das atrações a desfilar no Circuito Maneca Ferreira nesta quinta-feira (19), primeira noite da festa.
articles.body:
Milsinho, vocalista da banda Toque Dez, na Micareta de Feira de Santana 2026 — Foto: João Souza/g1

O arrocha tem conquistado cada vez mais espaço na Micareta de Feira de Santana . A cada ano, Milsinho, vocalista da banda Toque Dez , ganha ainda mais destaque no Circuito Maneca Ferreira, na Avenida Presidente Dutra, principal palco da festa que toma as ruas da segunda maior cidade da Bahia neste feriadão.

Em entrevista ao g1 , nesta quinta-feira (19), o cantor comemorou mais uma participação no evento e destacou o carinho do público feirense.

"Sempre falo: quando eu venho tocar aqui, eu me sinto em casa. Pelo carinho, pelo acolhimento da galera", afirmou.

O artista também adiantou novidades no repertório e contou que a banda pretende lançar um novo projeto em dezembro.

"Estaremos com muito arrocha, muita sofrência. Eu até falei que hoje vai ter repertório novo. A gente quer lançar agora um projeto, acho que dia 2 de dezembro. Então, hoje vai ser um show espetacular, um show à parte", reforçou.

Após a participação na micareta, na sexta-feira (20), o cantor tem apresentação marcada em Salvador, no projeto "Na Máxima".

A Micareta de Feira segue até o próximo domingo (22 ). Durante os dias de festa, estão previstos desfiles de artistas como Carlinhos Brown, Pedro Sampaio, Xanddy Harmonia, Tony Salles, Psirico, Léo Santana e Pablo.

Nesta primeira noite, além de Toque Dez, os foliões da cidade curtiram os desfiles de Claudia Leitte, Timbalada, Robyssão e muito mais.

articles.title: Robyssão lembra luta por liberdade de expressão no pagodão | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor celebrou o novo momento do ritmo em entrevista ao g1 nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana. Artista foi uma das atrações da festa, que se estende até domingo (22), no Circuito Maneca Ferreira.
articles.summary: Cantor celebrou o novo momento do ritmo em entrevista ao g1 nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana. Artista foi uma das atrações da festa.
articles.body:
Hoje um dos nomes mais experientes do pagodão baiano, Robyssão avalia que nem sempre os representantes do ritmo tiveram liberdade para cantar sobre diversos temas. O ex-vocalista do Balck Style ressalta que foi alvo de muitas críticas no passado por ousar com canções de duplo sentido.

"Eu fui um cara que recebi muitos bombardeios, porque minhas músicas sempre foram irreverentes, músicas de duplo sentido, e eu acho que isso que está acontecendo hoje é uma grande vitória".

A avaliação foi feita em entrevista ao g1 , nos bastidores da Micareta de Feira de Santana , na noite desta quinta-feira (19). Ele foi uma das primeiras atrações a comandar um trio no Circuito Maneca Ferreira, onde a festa segue até domingo (22).

Ao falar com o portal, Robyssão celebrou o novo momento vivido por artistas do gênero. "Tive que tomar muitas porradas para que artistas tivessem liberdade de expressão. (...) Lutei para que artistas pudessem abordar qualquer assunto, qualquer tema, sejam problemas sociais, sejam problemas relacionados a questões sexuais. Hoje, as pessoas têm liberdade, os artistas têm liberdade e podem abordar qualquer assunto, e isso é bom", destacou.

Robyssão foi uma das atrações da Micareta de Feira 2026 — Foto: João Souza/g1

Conhecido entre os fãs mais jovens como Tio Roby, o cantor também comentou sobre a surpresa de conquistar o público da geração Z, mesmo tendo construído a carreira em outra época.

"A coisa mais difícil que existe é você conquistar a geração Z, é quase que impossível. Eu sou das antigas, então é algo muito raro o que está acontecendo comigo: a geração Z consumir minhas músicas, frequentar meus shows e ainda me denominar como tio, tio Roby, né? Aí, daqui a um tempo, o que vai ser? Avô Roby, vovô Roby", brincou.

Em fevereiro de 2026, durante o Carnaval, Robyssão viralizou nas redes sociais ao comentar que vários artistas se envolveram em brigas e polêmicas durante a festa, enquanto ele não havia participado de nenhuma confusão.

Na entrevista, o cantor refletiu sobre essa postura. "Eu gosto de passar mensagens motivacionais, porque as pessoas andam às vezes perdidas, confusas, sobretudo os mais jovens. E a última mensagem que eu estou passando para essa turma mais jovem é para não desistir dos seus sonhos. Se você tem um sonho, lute. Não se arrependa, vá em frente. Se não der certo, pelo menos deu errado", aconselhou, em tom de brincadeira.

Carnaval fora de época recebe diversos artistas

Além de Robyssão, Claudia Leitte, Timbalada e Toque Dez estiveram entre as atrações desta primeira noite. A programação principal, até domingo, tem ainda diversos nomes como Pedro Sampaio e Michelle Andrade. Na segunda-feira (23), mais uma vez, Feira de Santana será palco para o "Arrastão", comandado por Thiago Aquino.

articles.title: Alonso: "Lo que recuerdo del Dakar es el dolor de cabeza, no puedes pestañear en 4 ó 5 horas"
articles.standfirst: Fernando explica en profundidad por qué ha dado el sí a la prueba más dura del motor y descarta la posibilidad de ganar el Rally... con la boca pequeña
articles.summary: Fernando explica en profundidad por qué ha dado el sí a la prueba más dura del motor y descarta la posibilidad de ganar el Rally... con la boca pequeña
articles.body: La rueda de prensa de Fernando Alonso en Las Vegas ha sido casi monográfica del Dakar, tras el reciente anuncio de que lo afrontará con Aston Martin este enero, siete años después de su primera participación. Como era natural, después de dos respuestas negativas en anteriores comparecencias respecto a participar el al clásico del desierto mientras se sigue en la F1, le recordaron sus propias palabras. "No creo que sea posible, es casi imposible", dijo en Singapur. "Sí, bueno, sigo pensando lo mismo; no he cambiado de opinión. Creo que el Dakar de 2027 será un desafío mucho mayor de lo que fue para mí en 2020. En aquel entonces tuve seis meses de preparación: fui a probar a distintos países, como Qatar, Namibia, Marruecos y Polonia; fue un programa bastante extenso. Además, creo que participé en dos rallies en Arabia Saudí. Ahora sólo tendré dos días en Marruecos y luego, ¡allá vamos! Es un periodo bastante corto, pero al final decidimos, junto con el equipo, Prodrive y Aston, que sigue siendo una buena experiencia para todas las partes, especialmente para mí, porque no es ningún secreto que algún día quiero ganar el Dakar. Este año no será posible, pero lo considero una inversión de cara al futuro: sumar más kilómetros y conocer mejor la disciplina", argumentaba el asturiano. Lo que quiere dejar claro es que sus expectativas son relativamente modestas y se lo toma como un aprendizaje para el futuro. "Creo que tiene sentido, es un mes en el que no hay mucha actividad en la F1. Es un coche divertido de conducir y resulta una experiencia gratificante, tanto en el plano profesional como en el personal. Como ya he dicho, es uno de los mayores retos, precisamente por la falta de preparación; aun así, intentaré realizar pruebas durante la primera semana y, con suerte, competir en la segunda", dice sobre el plan. Habla de la preparación como factor crucial y sus explicaciones sobre su experiencia de 2020 son más que interesantes. "Los pilotos que compiten allí llevan toda la vida haciéndolo. Se han criado en el mundo del automovilismo dentro de los rallies y con este tipo de vehículos; saben interpretar los distintos terrenos, los matices, las variaciones en la luz...", desmenuzaba. "En el Dakar hay muchísimos aspectos que son totalmente diferentes. En la F1, en un circuito, se trata de repetir lo mismo una vuelta tras otra, tratando de perfeccionar el estilo de conducción. En los rallies, todo consiste en improvisar; improvisar constantemente, porque no sabes qué va a pasar en el siguiente metro. Una de mis fortalezas siempre ha sido la capacidad de adaptarme rápidamente a las situaciones y a los cambios, pero esto es otro nivel. Recuerdo que, durante mis primeras jornadas de pruebas en el Dakar, terminaba por la noche con dolor de cabeza", rememoraba. "Creo que se debe al nivel de concentración que requiere, algo a lo que no estoy acostumbrado. No puedes ni parpadear durante cuatro o cinco horas. En cambio, aquí [en la Fórmula 1], ajustamos parámetros en el volante, nos comunicamos por radio, observamos las pantallas y seguimos la carrera; al fin y al cabo, te mantienes en un entorno reducido, vuelta tras vuelta", compara entre ambas disciplinas. "En el Dakar, te adentras en lo desconocido. Cada metro es nuevo. Dada mi trayectoria, el desafío es mayor que para alguien que no se ha formado en esta disciplina", añadía. Sobre sus opciones de éxito, prefiere la cautela y se remite a la experiencia de uno de sus compañeros en Aston Martin para 2027. "No sé... creo que he demostrado ser competitivo, pero, como mencioné, en su momento conté con unos seis meses de preparación y varios miles de kilómetros de pruebas previos, algo de lo que ahora no dispongo. Mi compañero de equipo actual, Sébastien Loeb, es probablemente el mejor piloto de rallies de la historia. Ha participado en el Dakar nueve o diez veces y aún no ha logrado la victoria. Soy consciente de la dificultad, pero precisamente por eso resulta tan atractivo: es un desafío enorme. Para Fernando lo crucial es esa dificultad que entraña asumir el desafío. "Por eso es interesante y por eso quiero intentar ganarlo algún día. Sí. No, eso no ha cambiado. El Dakar siempre ha estado presente en mis planes. También Le Mans y las 500 Millas de Indianápolis...", recalca. "Me encanta competir. Me apasiona pilotar coches de carreras: pisas el acelerador y sientes la potencia; pisas el freno y experimentas la deceleración. Son sensaciones que, hoy en día, echamos de menos en la Fórmula 1, por eso pensaba en todo esto. Por supuesto, al continuar en la Fórmula 1 esa será siempre mi prioridad y resulta complicado compaginarla con otros programas. El Dakar, al celebrarse en enero, encaja algo mejor, aunque también han tenido que darse ciertas circunstancias", especificaba. Fernando explicaba de dónde salió este proyecto y cómo se concretó. "Creo que esto fue allá por julio. David Richards vino, probablemente durante la carrera en Silverstone, y ya tuvimos esa conversación; aunque, en aquel momento, ni siquiera se planteó la participación. Él simplemente estaba allí con Prodrive. Así que le dije: 'No lo sé, David; no sé qué pasará el año que viene'". Estaba claro que en ese momento la retirada de la F1 seguía siendo una posibilidad. "Al final, todo encajó rápidamente; estoy contento y preparado para aprender tanto como sea posible", añadía Alonso sobre lo que viene. Con tan corta preparación y ante la magnitud del reto, le cuestionaron sobre si sel Dakar supone ponerse en peligro. No se dice la palabra accidente, pero se sobreentiende. "No, en absoluto", zanjaba. ¿Y qué dijeron en Aston Martin?: "Estuvieron encantados. Saben que necesito conducir algo... Piloto todas las semanas, varias cosas. A veces, como ya he comentado en alguna ocasión, piloto coches de Fórmula 1. que ni siquiera son Aston Martin ni nada por el estilo, y en este caso, al menos, se trata de la misma marca y los mismos colores". Fernando descarta que no tenga el control a bordo de un coche del Dakar. "Tengo el control total del coche. Lo que no controlo del todo es la velocidad a la que me acerco a los peligros. Por ejemplo, cuando voy con un copiloto excelente como Marc Coma, a veces, tras recorrer quizá 10 kilómetros a fondo en medio de la nada, él divisa a lo lejos un poco de vegetación o algo verde; siempre me avisa: 'Si ves algo verde, prepárate, que vienen baches'", decía con tono humorístico. "Así que voy aprendiendo estas cosas sobre la marcha, gracias a su experiencia. Supongo que, para otros pilotos, todo esto es algo automático porque ya han pasado por situaciones similares. Por tanto, estoy en un proceso de aprendizaje acelerado, justo en plena carrera. Pero, como piloto, me resulta fascinante", aseguraba. Si en su cabeza sigue la idea de completar la Triple Corona y volver a Indianápolis, Fernando duda. Pues no lo sé. "Van a cambiar los coches pronto. Algún día... bueno, creo que el año que viene. Llega un coche nuevo. Así que, no sé... quizá algún día me lo plantee. No está en mis planes a corto plazo, no lo tengo en mente ahora mismo, pero no puedo decir que sea un 'no' rotundo", deslizaba En cuanto al rumor de hacer también las 24 Horas de Le Mans en 2027, Fernando contestaba: "No, por el momento sólo la F1 y el Dakar". Es un no, pero no lo niega definitivamente tampoco.

articles.title: Paul Nicholls breaks record for National Hunt wins after surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time tally with Warwick triumph
articles.summary: Ditcheat handler Paul Nicholls became the winning-most trainer in British National Hunt history, surpassing the great Martin Pipe's total of 3,390 when Knappers Hill crossed the line in front at Lingfield, donning the colours of Paul Barber
articles.body:
The 14-time champion eclipsed Pipe's record of 3,930 wins at Warwick on Thursday after Knappers Hill toughed out victory in the Denis O'Connell Memorial Veterans' Handicap Chase under Sam Twiston-Davies, carrying the colours of the trainer's long-time friend and mentor Paul Barber.

Nicholls, who has been training at Manor Farm Stables in Somerset since 1991 after first renting the yard from Barber, was thrilled to etch his name into the history of a sport in which he has long been a master of his craft.

"I never thought when I started training we'd ever train that many winners, but it's a nice milestone," said Nicholls, whose tally includes famous victories by all-time great horses such as Kauto Star, Big Buck's and Denman.

"We're not far off 4,000 winners that have been sent out across all codes, but they'll get beaten again in the future because records are always there to be broken.

"You'd probably have thought Martin would never have been beaten. What a fantastic trainer he was.

"Hopefully we can head on with the British winners and end up with getting near the 4,000. It's exciting."

Nicholls added: "As you keep racking up these winners, you're getting closer and closer.

"A year ago, I wouldn't have known the exact number, but then, of course, everyone fills you in and now you know.

"It's just a target, isn't it? Dan [Skelton] is targeting beating Martin's record of winners in a season. We all like beating records.

"It's nice to be the winning-most National Hunt trainer in Britain, even if it's not forever, it's nice to do that. It just reflects well on the whole team at Ditcheat and the whole set-up really and what we've done here."

Olveston has more meaning than most for Nicholls as it is not only the village where he was raised, but it is also the name of his first winner.

What made it even more special was his father Brian was a part-owner and family has been a running theme throughout his 35 years at Manor Farm, with daughters Megan and Olive and nephew Harry Derham all playing their part along the way.

He added: "I remember my first winner. It was December 20, 1991 at Hereford. Dad was involved in Olveston with some mates. It was brilliant.

"Megan's had a lot of winners, Olive has, Harry Derham was here and dad's still here every day.

"I've been incredibly lucky, I've had some great people around me, some fantastic horses. We keep trying to work hard and do the best we can.

"Paul Barber was a big part of my life and lots of people along the way. Lots of people have gone on to be good jockeys, lots of people have been gone on to be great trainers.

"It's just been a fantastic journey. I pinch myself to think I've been here 35 years now, it just seems like it was yesterday. I don't know where time goes."

As he targets his next landmark, what remaining ambitions does Nicholls have for a trainer who has won it all?

"Keep training winners, still loving the game. I love the game. It's just awesome," said Nicholls, who is still one short of Pipe's 15 champion trainer titles.

"I've invested quite heavily in some new facilities this year, I've got some nice young horses and a good team around me. I love it, just training big winners."

images.caption: Image: Paul Nicholls has trained more National Hunt winners than any other handler

articles.title: Paul Nicholls: Breaks Martin Pipe’s all-time National Hunt tally for winners by a British trainer
articles.summary: Paul Nicholls surpasses Martin Pipe to set a new National Hunt record for winners by a British trainer.
articles.body:
Paul Nicholls has surpassed Martin Pipe to set a new National Hunt record for winners by a British trainer.

The 14-time champion claimed his 3,931st win at Warwick on Thursday as Knappers Hill secured victory in the Denis O'Connell Memorial Veterans' Handicap Chase.

Since starting as a trainer in 1991, Nicholls has gone on to look after some legendary horses such as Kauto Star, Big Buck's and Denman.

"I never thought when I started training we'd ever train that many winners, but it's a nice milestone," said the 64-year-old.

"We're not far off 4,000 winners that have been sent out across all codes, but they'll get beaten again in the future because records are always there to be broken.

"You'd probably have thought Martin would never have been beaten. What a fantastic trainer he was.

"Hopefully we can head on with the British winners and end up with getting near the 4,000. It's exciting."

Nicholls' first winner came in December 1991 with Olveston - a horse with the same name as the Gloucestershire village he grew up and was part-time owned by his father.

From there he went from strength to strength, training four Cheltenham Gold Cup winners and had Grand National success with Neptune Collonges in 2012.

"It's nice to be the winning-most National Hunt trainer in Britain, even if it's not forever, it's nice to do that," added the Somerset-based Nicholls.

"It just reflects well on the whole team at Ditcheat and the whole set-up really and what we've done here."

articles.title: Jorge Martín: "No voy a ser el que vaya a tirar a Marc Márquez, no todo vale"
articles.standfirst: No da todo por perdido, aunque es realista
articles.summary: No da todo por perdido, aunque es realista
articles.body: Jorge Martín es más que consciente de sus pocas opciones de mantener vivo el Mundial de MotoGP 2026 en el Gran Premio de Portugal, en Portimao. Eso sí, advierte que está ya casi a tope físicamente, sin molestias en el radio de la muñeca derecha. Considera un orgullo haber peleado, y pelear, con Marc Márquez. "Posible es, eso está claro, pero no está en mi control. Mi control sólo está en intentar ganar las cuatro carreras que quedan y es lo que voy a intentar. Estar muy concentrado en hacer bien lo que sé hacer, que es ir en moto, en pilotar. Está claro que no puedo controlar lo que él haga, así que todo puede pasar. Estoy en MotoGP y en el deporte todo puede pasar, pero no está en mi control. Es muy difícil, pero posibilidades sí que hay". "Si no estoy al 100%, estoy muy cerca. Tengo un poco de dolor, pero creo que la moto no me va a condicionar para nada, así que estoy preparado. Creo que he hecho un gran trabajo esta semana; me ha venido muy bien descansar, con ganas de ver mi potencial al 100%, de volver a coger la pila que está funcionando muy bien. Y aparte, en dos pistas donde ganaron el año pasado, creo que podemos hacer un buen trabajo". "Es verdad que ha sido inoportuna, pero mirando un poco con perspectiva, Marc ha tenido una lesión, Marco ha tenido una lesión y yo he tenido una lesión; al final hemos empatado. Obviamente, es una pena, pero mirando con perspectiva, a principio de año no me podía poner el mono y estoy a falta de dos carreras peleando por ganar un Mundial. Estar aquí ya es una victoria y voy a intentar todo lo que pueda para alargarlo. Pero yo no voy a ser el que vaya a tirar a Marc y luego intentar ganar porque, para mí, no todo vale, vale estar concentrado, intentar ganar el sábado, intentar ganar el domingo y luego, si algo pasa y me llega la oportunidad ahí estaré para cogerla". "Me da igual. Está claro que es mejor tercero que cuarto y segundo que tercero, pero el valor de un subcampeonato o un tercero para mí es el mismo; al final es no ser campeón. No es algo que esté en mi mente; quizá otros pilotos lo tienen en mente, pero no es mi caso. Yo intentaré pelear por ganar por mí, por acabar bien con Aprilia, para acabar bien estos dos años que no han sido fáciles y al final he conseguido rehacerme como piloto. Lo que tenga que ser, pues será". "Yo creo que todo el año he ido un poco con la mochila de no haber corrido el año pasado y quizá en Austria empecé a encontrarme mejor. Fue cuando ya por fin me encontraba ahí para pelear y estaba en la pelea. Está claro que es una pena, pero en Australia fallé y eso ha provocado que ahora las opciones del mundial sean mucho más lejanas. De todas formas, me quedo con estar peleando con uno de los mejores pilotos de la historia, si no el mejor, a su mejor nivel; él mismo lo ha dicho, y estoy aquí peleando contra él. Eso al final me demuestra mi valor y creo que es un privilegio y estoy muy orgulloso de lo que estoy consiguiendo". "Al final, he pasado mucho, pero Marc también ha pasado mucho. Creo que cada persona o cada piloto tiene su mochila. Al ser más conocidos o por la fama, se sabe todo de nosotros, pero creo que todo el mundo tiene su lucha personal. Esta ha sido la mía y está claro que si puedo ayudar a gente a que siga luchando y ayudar a gente a que salga de un momento duro, pues yo encantado". "Si en parte lo hago, también es por esto, por ayudar a gente que me escribe, que está con enfermedades crónicas, que lo está pasando muy mal y aún por verme correr, por ver que después con el brazo roto sigo luchando y eso al final le da mucho valor a mi trabajo".

articles.title: FIA announce introduction of full-time F1 stewards from 2027 ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix
articles.summary: Formula 1's governing body, the FIA, has revealed full-time stewards will be used for the first time from next year; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with Friday's practice sessions at 12.30am and 4pm
articles.body:
The use of full-time stewards has been a consistent talking point in F1 as different stewards, who adjudicate all racing and technical matters on a race weekend, are used at each event over the season.

There has been an argument that this can lead to inconsistencies in decision-making when it comes to imposing penalties, or the severity of a penalty.

But the FIA announced on Thursday, ahead of this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, they will begin to recruit full-time stewards with a phased introduction from next year with the aim of establishing 12-15 full-time stewards over the coming years.

Currently, there are four stewards drawn from a large FIA pool of officials and one of those is a former racing driver. The new structure will continue to use the knowledge of driver stewards at each event and the FIA say full-time stewards will "allow for deeper implementation of best practice and greater consistency in decision-making".

The news comes a month after the opening of the FIA Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill in the UK, following a reorganisation of Race Control in 2022 after the controversial 2021 season which saw Max Verstappen overtake Lewis Hamilton on the last lap of the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

"This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport," said FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem.

"The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport.

"Following the milestone opening of the new FIA Remote Operations Centre and strengthening of officiating development through initiatives such as the FIA High Performance Programme, this development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships."

articles.title: F1 to introduce full-time race stewards from 2027
articles.summary: Formula 1's governing body the FIA is to introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Formula 1's governing body the FIA is to introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season.

The move follows consistent calls from grand prix drivers for the change because of criticisms of inconsistency of decisions regarding penalties for on-track incidents.

The FIA said in a statement that it would begin recruiting permanent stewards, and was planning a "phased introduction" during the 2027 season.

The FIA statement added: "The introduction of dedicated full-time stewards to the FIA's flagship championship will provide continuity and expertise within the stewarding structure, further advancing the FIA's commitment to fairness through the ongoing review and continuous improvement of sporting regulations and stewarding guidelines.

"It will also allow for deeper implementation of best practice and greater consistency in decision-making."

It said that the use of driver stewards, usually an ex-F1 driver, would continue, "recognising the invaluable expertise they bring".

The plan is for "a small number" of full-time stewards to be recruited during 2027 and the group to be expanded from 2028.

"Existing FIA stewards will continue to play a vital role, contributing their experience within a mixed roster of full-time and part-time stewards for the foreseeable future," the statement said.

In reality, the move is not a major step on from the current situation, where a small number of stewards are rotated around races.

Each grand prix has a group of four stewards, one of which is an ex-driver.

Current drivers have often referenced the fact that they had repeatedly complained during briefings with FIA officials that rulings on driver standards and racing errors were not applied on a consistent basis.

Last year, Williams driver Carlos Sainz, a director of drivers' body the Grand Prix Drivers' Association, said: "F1 and the FIA all agree that [permanent stewards] should be the way forward, where at least two of the three stewards are permanent and we have one rotational for teaching purposes."

The decision follows the opening of an FIA race operations centre at F1's Biggin Hill headquarters in south London.

The FIA has in recent years received increased income from F1 - which provides the majority of its funding - on the basis that this would be applied to improving officialdom and rule-making.

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said: "This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport.

"The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula 1 World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport."

articles.title: Could IndyCar return to Kansas? Series testing the waters on oval
articles.summary: IndyCar drivers Pato O'Ward and Will Power are testing at Kansas Speedway, fueling rumors of a potential return in 2027.
articles.body:
Four weeks after IndyCar announced its 2027 schedule , the series is testing the waters at a track not on the schedule. On Friday, Arrow McLaren's Pato O'Ward and Andretti Global's Will Power will drive on the Kansas Speedway oval in Kansas City, Kansas.

Per an IndyCar spokesperson, it is an aerodynamic validation test as the series "gathers information and data in the event an opportunity arises to race on the 1.5-mile oval in the future." IndyCar declined to reveal whether the future could be as soon as 2027.

IndyCar hasn't raced at Kansas Speedway since 2010. The series raced at the track for a decade after it opened in 2001, but hasn't returned since.

IndyCar hasn't visited Kansas Speedway in any capacity since the introduction of its current Dallara DW12 chassis in 2012, thus the need to test the current aerodynamic package at the track. It's worth noting that 2027 is slated to be the final year of the DW12, as Dallara's IR28 will debut in 2028 after it went through a series of validation tests this year. Testing the current car would suggest that IndyCar has interest in racing at the track in 2027.

IndyStar's best photos from the 110th running of the Indianapolis 500

When Nashville Superspeedway was removed from IndyCar's schedule in October, it left the series with four oval tracks (and five races) in 2027. IndyCar president Doug Boles claimed losing Nashville was "something that none of us want to see" and that finding additional ovals was a "big priority" for the series .

"The question really becomes, how can we go into a market where the attendance will make it feel like an event?" Boles asked. "I think that's really important to us to get into that. Where do we have a promoter that doesn't just want us, but is willing to promote alongside us and really be that lead in that community to help drive the attendance is an important piece of that. ... There's a significant number of tracks, like I said, that would have interest. It's just a matter now of finding the right one where we think we can have the most success, where we can create the racing that we're so known for on the ovals."

If IndyCar races at Kansas in 2027, it seems likely that it'd be in tandem with NASCAR, which owns the track. NASCAR has two Cup Series races at Kansas in 2027, with one being in its postseason "The Chase." The other race is slated for Sunday, May 9.

There exists a world where IndyCar holds a race at Kansas the day before the Cup Series race. In March, IndyCar returned to Phoenix Raceway, another NASCAR-owned oval, for a Saturday-Sunday doubleheader. IndyCar and NASCAR will repeat that doubleheader in 2027 , signifying a growing relationship between America's two major motorsports series.

"We wouldn't be opposed to looking at other oval tracks where we could partner together," Boles told IndyStar in March . "The biggest challenge in it is (the) schedule and finding a date on the schedule that works for both NASCAR and IndyCar."

If IndyCar does go to Kansas in May, it would add to an already jam-packed month. Teams would go straight from the Indianapolis 500 open test on May 4 and 5 to Kansas before returning to Indianapolis Motor Speedway for the Sonsio Grand Prix on May 15. That would lead straight into the two weeks of Indy 500 practice and qualifying and the Indy 500 (May 30) before the series races on the streets of Detroit (June 6) and World Wide Technology Raceway (June 13).

The grind of May and early June already drew the ire of some in the paddock , and another race could make that worse. At the same time, the series had success – both attendance-wise and via televison viewership – partnering with NASCAR in 2026, and it may not be a bad idea to do so twice in 2027.

IndyCar has kept its schedule at 17 races or fewer in recent years, with 2026 being the exception. (Washington, D.C.'s Freedom 250 Grand Prix was a late addition in January after President Donald Trump signed an executive order to have the race.) Mark Miles, the CEO and president of IndyCar parent company Penske Entertainment, said going beyond 17 races has been a discussion between him and Penske Entertainment chairman Roger Penske.

"We need to make sure that it makes economic sense for the series and for the teams," Miles said. "The team owners, it costs them to race. So we got to bring some more revenue in. But when things are done in an orchestrated way, I think there's potential."

For now, IndyCar is just seeing how its car would run on Kansas Speedway's progressive banking oval. If O'Ward and Power's test goes well, it could lead to another late addition to the calendar. The track will not be open to the public for the test.

Zion Brown is IndyStar's motorsports reporter. Follow him at @z10nbr0wn . Get IndyStar's motor sports coverage sent directly to your inbox with our Motor Sports newsletter . Subscribe to the YouTube channel IndyStar TV: IndyCar for a behind-the-scenes look at IndyCar and expert analysis .
